transcript: A few nights ago, I saw Bedlam's world premiere new musical called Music City by best-selling country songwriter J.T. Harding and playwright Peter Zinn. This is a story about everyday people trying to get discovered, get clean, or just get by. It's not your typical musical for a number of reasons, but in theatrical terms, it's kind of like Once but in Tennessee. The actors do a lot of self-accompaniment and oftentimes assume band membership when they're not acting in a scene. I was really impressed by the multi-instrumentalists and there's so much musical talent packed into a pretty small ensemble. The characters easy to latch onto and although the plot felt at times a little rushed, the music is the beating heart of the show and provides a solid emotional arc to the story. The music is very good from soaring ballads to country bangers, and the way the songs are performed is gritty, raw, and passionate. The staging is immersive and there's no bad seat in the house which they've converted into an open mic bar called The Wicked Tickle. This brings a strong sense of atmosphere and authenticity that helps contribute to the performances feeling loose and spontaneous. And I'm not really a country music person, but I thought this was a very exciting piece. It’s still in previews and a little rough around the edges, but I think they've got something here. Music City is currently running at the West End Theatre on the Upper West Side through December 1st, but I hope this is not the last production of it that we see. With that, other program for my collection.
